log_directory.description: Absolute path to the directory where pgAudit log files will be written. Must be writable by the PostgreSQL user.

log_filename.description: Base filename for audit logs. Supports standard strftime-style placeholders for timestamps and user.

log_rotation_age.description: Maximum age (in seconds) of a log file before rotation. Set to 0 to disable time-based rotation.

log_rotation_size.description: Maximum size (in MB) of a log file before rotation. Set to 0 to disable size-based rotation.

log_rotation_max_files.description: Maximum number of old (including compressed) log files to retain. Older files are deleted on rotation.

log_compression.description: Whether to compress rotated log files using gzip to save disk space.

min_messages.description: Minimum message level to include in the audit log (e.g., LOG, ERROR, FATAL). Lower levels include more detail.

debug_redirector.description: Enable verbose internal logging of the pgAudit redirector module for troubleshooting.

items.description: Category or type of SQL events to audit. Common options: 'read', 'write', 'ddl', 'function', 'role', 'admin', 'relation'.

audit_events.description: List of event categories to capture. Adjust based on your compliance and security requirements.

items.description: Name of a PostgreSQL role to exclude from auditing. Use for internal/system accounts.

exclude_roles.description: List of role names that should not be audited (e.g., superusers or service accounts).

items.description: Name of a schema to exclude from auditing.

exclude_schemas.description: List of schema names that should not be audited. Useful for system schemas.

log_file_mode.description: Octal permission mode for new log files (e.g., 0640 = 420 in decimal). Must be readable by PostgreSQL user and group.

log_file_owner.description: Unix username that will own the log files (usually the PostgreSQL service account).

log_file_group.description: Unix group that will own the log files. Ensure this group has appropriate access.

max_log_writers.description: Maximum number of background writer processes to handle concurrent log writes. Increase for very high-traffic databases.

enabled.description: Toggle to enable or disable pgAudit log redirection entirely.
